exclusions.reason: Organisation/contact/background details are low-priority descriptive context without a distinct material quantitative premise.
examples: Membership and group counts, brands and services; institutional contacts.

exclusions.reason: Preferences, fairness evaluations, rhetorical characterisations and unbounded future effects are not independently testable factual findings.
examples: Horizontal policy is fairer; selective relief is unjustified; general tax reduction preferred; long-term rule-based subsidy desired; fixed subsidy is inadequate for planning.

exclusions.reason: Future annual cost, per-kWh relief and investment outcomes are conditional forecasts; only their explicit arithmetic/structural premises are inventoried.
examples: Growing future cost base and decreasing future relief per kWh; future electrification attractiveness and economic viability.

exclusions.reason: Cover and organisational/contact/profile information has no additional material cost/benefit/legal premise.
examples: Author date, addresses, registry numbers and rounded membership/employment profile.

exclusions.reason: Preferences, business-value judgments and forecasts are excluded; factual duration, tax, mechanism and pass-through premises are retained.
examples: Competitive prices are important; subsidy is insufficient; structural reform needed; financing is politically fragile; possible burden jump after 2029.

exclusions.reason: Organisational profile and rhetorical prioritisation are low-priority context.
examples: Over 5000 members; electricity price is the central competitive lever.

exclusions.reason: Requested amounts and financing reforms are normative; future investment, transformation and price effects are forecasts.
examples: Keep €6.5bn; move levies into federal budget; strengthen competitiveness and avoid delaying electrification.

exclusions.reason: Policy requests and unquantified fears about future reforms are judgments/forecasts.
examples: Permanent competitive tariffs; closer regulator/government coordination; reform may shift costs against industry; delete §24d(6).

exclusions.reason: Organisational economic profile and contacts are low-priority descriptive background, not separate material policy premises.
examples: Staff/contact details, member count, sector turnover/employment.

exclusions.reason: Policy priorities and future harm/benefit forecasts are excluded while material numerical, legal and present-policy premises are retained.
examples: Public ownership preferred; energy poverty/deindustrialisation risks; electricity prices should be lower; stabilisation and further measures demanded.

exclusions.reason: References to DGB’s own previous advocacy are not independent external factual premises merely because footnoted.
examples: Previous positions on industrial price, StromVKG, EEG and grid reform; contact information.

exclusions.reason: Proposed stabilisation account design, desired targets, guardrails and future policy benefits are normative proposals.
examples: 2025 target corridor; minimum account funding, reserve and federal guarantee; public top-up, annual reports, ten-year planning horizon, voluntary flexibility.

exclusions.reason: Conditional technical examples are checked only as conditional arithmetic, not manufactured predictions; contacts and institutional statements are low-priority.
examples: 5%,10%,15% cost scenarios; exact future bills and investments; Good Work and transformation priorities.
